title: Métricas de resiliencia y BIA
description: Recovery objectives, reliability metrics, quantitative risk formulas, and recovery site types.
rows: RTO (Recovery Time Objective)
Maximum acceptable time to restore a service after a disruption.
Determines site type and recovery method: a short RTO needs a hot site or high availability.
RTO is about downtime; RPO is about data loss. Do not swap them.
RPO (Recovery Point Objective)
Maximum acceptable amount of data loss, expressed as time since the last good copy.
Backup or replication interval must be at or below the RPO (RPO of 1 hour means at least hourly backups).
A question about how often to back up is an RPO question.
MTTR (Mean Time to Repair/Recover)
Average time needed to restore a failed component or system.
MTTR = total repair time / number of repairs. Lower is better.
MTTR must fit within the RTO, otherwise the objective cannot be met.
MTBF (Mean Time Between Failures)
Average operating time between failures of a repairable component.
MTBF = total operating time / number of failures. Higher is better.
MTBF applies to repairable items; MTTF applies to items that are replaced.
MTTF (Mean Time to Failure)
Average expected lifetime of a non-repairable component.
Higher is better; used to plan replacements and spares.
Do not use MTTF for something that gets repaired.
EF (Exposure Factor)
Percentage of an asset's value lost in one occurrence of a threat.
Expressed from 0 to 100% (or 0.0 to 1.0).
EF is a percentage, not a dollar amount.
SLE (Single Loss Expectancy)
Monetary loss from a single occurrence.
SLE = AV (asset value) x EF.
Calculate SLE before ALE.
ARO (Annualized Rate of Occurrence)
Expected number of occurrences per year.
Once every 4 years = 0.25; three times a year = 3.
Convert the frequency to a per-year figure before multiplying.
ALE (Annualized Loss Expectancy)
Expected loss per year from a risk.
ALE = SLE x ARO.
A control is cost-justified when its annual cost is lower than the ALE reduction it provides.
Hot site
Fully equipped alternate site with current data, ready to take over almost immediately.
Minutes to hours to switch over; highest cost.
Pick it when the RTO is very short and cost is not the main constraint.
Warm site
Alternate site with hardware and connectivity but not current data or full configuration.
Hours to days to become operational; moderate cost.
The usual middle-ground answer balancing cost and recovery time.
Cold site
Space with power and cooling only; equipment and data must be brought in.
Days to weeks to become operational; lowest cost.
Cheapest option but cannot meet short RTOs.
Geographic dispersion
Placing alternate sites far enough apart that one regional event cannot affect both.
Distance should exceed the expected footprint of regional disasters.
A backup site in the same flood zone or power grid does not provide resilience.
